# Cartoon Fun Facts 卡通冷知识 — Style Prompt
Status: draft (not yet approved by the user). Skill: 卡通冷知识短片 (skill-1793643373152). Kit: /workspace/shared/cartoon-facts-kit/

## 1. Essence, and what it is not
Vertical 1080×1920 flat 2D cartoon fun-fact short (30–35 s). One fact per line, one funny metaphor each; hook question shown on screen at once; the ending flips the hook into a gag. Not realistic, not slow push-ins on stills, no characters baked into backgrounds.
## 2. Materials & rendering
Thick dark-brown outlines, flat fills + simple cel shading, big eyes, vector feel. Characters are cutouts (9 poses: neutral, shout, shock, blush, heart-eyes, sweat, attack, wilted, sidekick) moving over 9 illustrated empty backgrounds (base scale 1.2). Floating motes, vignette.
## 3. Colour logic
Hero has its own palette clearly separated from background props. Keyword yellow #ffd21f with ink stroke; red marker for circles/arrows. No gradient text.
## 4. Type & subtitles
ZCOOL KuaiLe 站酷快乐体 (OFL). White pill caption bar at y=1470, 60–64 px, 2–4 characters per block, one yellow keyword per block. Big title at y=430, spring-in then wobble, no full stop. No emoji.
## 5. Motion quality
Nothing still for 1 s; a new action every 0.5–1 s inside a shot. Idle float, squash on pose change, speed lines on entry, starburst hit + shake, zoom punch 1.1. Every cut, pose, title and SFX is cued on real word timings (iron rule: element moves when the keyword is spoken).
## 6. Camera grammar
Hard cut every 1.5–3 s; each fact gets a new background and a new pose.
## 7. Sound palette
Fish Audio drama-3 科普男声, ~4.2–4.5 字/s; BGM ≈ −12 dB with sidechain, ~9 dB under voice; synthesized SFX (sfx_mix.py); total −14 LUFS.
## 8. Native moves
Red marker circle, curved red arrow, yellow/white starburst, 28-slice swim wobble, props in character local space.
## 9. Pitfalls of the medium
Grid-line slicing cuts neighbour limbs; white fringes; black edge at bottom when scaled; starburst too small turns to black ball; yuvj420p output; hero too small (+20%). No clipping/穿模.
## 10. Engine
Single HTML canvas, frame = pure function of t, window.seek/READY/END/EV; Playwright + system Chrome, 30 fps × 6 motion-blur subframes → ffmpeg. Final renders on the Mac mini.
## 11. Variation space / known gaps
Backgrounds generated at low resolution look soft; English version uses Luckiest Guy. Only the 0–15 s opening has been made so far.

## Rules for making a film in this style (user rules)
1. BGM teardown HTML review page first; wait for the human's explicit「通过」.
2. Script + shot plan to the user first; no image gen / voice / spending before confirmation.
3. Make only the 0–15 s opening first; self-review ≥ 90/100 before showing.
4. No clipping (不穿模).
5. Deliver only one 1080p release (H.264 CRF 18–20, yuv420p tv range, AAC) + one preview < 10 MB. Covers 4:3 and 3:4 only.
6. All rendering on the Mac mini. Facts need two independent sources.

# Direct-Etched Film 胶片直刻 — Style Prompt

> Lines scratched straight into dark film stock, dyed by hand, glowing on projection.
> Source: style study of Lemomo *THE NIGHT CLIMB* (https://x.com/lemomo_ai/status/2116717173934825841) — style learning only; never reuse its footage, frames, characters or story.

## 1. Essence, and what it is not
A dark, warm-black film frame where every drawing is an **engraved warm-white line**, and each subject carries **one saturated dye** laid in hatching that glows. Everything is redrawn **on twos**, so lines, dye and scratches boil together: it feels hand-made and projected.

Not: a neon/cyberpunk glow look (no clean vector lines, no gradients), not a "vintage film" filter over footage (no sprocket holes, no frame borders, no sepia), not flat motion graphics, not chalkboard (lines are thin and luminous, ground is warm black, not green/grey).

## 2. Materials & rendering
- Ground: warm black `#130f10`; mean frame luma ≈ 29/255, lit area only 1–17 % of the frame.
- Line: warm white `#f5efe2`, median width ≈ 2 px @1080 (detail), outlines 4–10 px; line ends left open, pressure varies.
- Dye: per subject, −60° parallel hatching over a translucent base of the same colour that **spills past the outline**.
- Overlaps brighten (additive / screen), never darken.
- Glow: 6–10 px blur bloom on lines and dye.
- Film damage: many short curved white hair scratches + dust specks, **20–40 per redraw, re-scattered every redraw**.
- Vignette + a warm light leak. No sprocket holes, no frame border.

## 3. Colour logic
- Constants: warm black ground, warm white line.
- **One subject = one dye**: cyan `#3be6d6`, blue `#3585e2`, red `#df3e30`, gold `#e7bc27`. Never two dyes on one subject; never a large dye area that out-weighs the lead (keep secondary fills small).
- The accent the story follows gets the most saturated dye; dim non-leads to 40–60 %.

## 4. Type & subtitles
- Subtitles: warm white, light weight, small glow, bottom centre, never over the lead.
- On-screen words are etched like lines (stroke reveal), not pasted type. Size floors from the director rules (main ≥120 px, sub ≥56, label ≥34 @1080).

## 5. Motion quality
- Boil **on twos**: random seed = floor(frame/2). Lemomo measured at 15 redraws/s; our 24 fps test is 12/s (15/s needs 30 fps — decide per film).
- Motion slow and sparse; one lead at a time, ≤3 moving regions.
- **Keyword hit rule**: the element tied to a spoken keyword moves on that word (±1 frame) with a clearly visible change. Never let the boil hide a weak hit (e.g. test's 「他」 Δ+2 is too weak).

## 6. Camera grammar
- Mostly locked or slow push; hard cuts between ideas; left/right split screen for comparison (you vs him).

## 7. Sound palette
- Loudness −14 LUFS integrated, true peak ≤ −1.5 dBTP. Reference ran ≈129 BPM; motion does not need to sit on beats (reference r = −0.07), but keyword hits must sit on speech.
- No whispering, no sudden silence (user rule).

## 8. Native moves
- Hard cut (reference cuts at 14.30 / 23.37 / 30.97 s).
- Left/right split screen for comparisons (reference 15–31 s).
- A line etching itself in, then being dyed with hatching.

## 9. Pitfalls of the medium
- Too much dye area (the test's quilt) steals the lead.
- Hatching too sparse loses the scratched feel; keep it dense, with dark gaps.
- Thin lines vanish at small sizes (mosquitoes): thicken small subjects' outlines.
- Even, uniform glow looks digital; vary it.
- Unseeded randomness breaks parallel rendering.

## 10. Engine
- Canvas 2D hand-drawn per frame + post compositing (glow, scratches, vignette, leak) in the same page; every frame a pure function of t; seeded randomness.
- Render: on the cloud box ≤2 workers (software WebGL, 8 cores); **official renders on the Mac mini** (user rule 2026-11-01).
- H.264 yuv420p bt709 tv, faststart.

## 11. Variation space / known gaps for next version
- Characters: move from round-head stick figures to designed characters with expressions.
- Denser hatching with black gaps; smaller dye areas; varied glow.
- Boil 15/s (30 fps) vs 12/s (24 fps) to decide.
- Add graphic language (rulers, ticks, diagrams) of our own.

# 光点粒子 Breathing Light Particles — STYLE (invariants only)
Learned from Lemomo's 光点粒子 post (style study only). Measurements: /workspace/mosquito-film/styletest2/dots/REPORT.md.

## 1. Essence
Night picture-book. Every subject (people, animals, land, moon, grass) is a cloud of soft glowing dots on near-black. Dots breathe; subjects form by gathering and leave by scattering. Best for lyrical / character stories, nature, night, crowds, migration. **Not**: steps, numbers, dense facts, product UI.
## 2. Materials & rendering
Additive point sprites (bright white core → coloured halo → transparent), `lighter` blending so overlaps brighten. Core radius median 3.5 px @1080 (p25 3.0, p90 5.0); a few big "firefly" dots 1.5×. Extra glow pass: ¼-res blur ≈ 6–10 px @1080 added at 0.5. Faint coloured haze behind dense areas. Vignette.
## 3. Colour
Ground near-black with a cool-green cast, rgb ≈ (4–11, 5–13, 8–12), mean frame luma 12–38/255, pixels >90 only 0.3–12 %. Two-family palette: warm gold/cream for characters, moon, light (#f0dba0 / #e5e3d2 / #c2b28e); muted sage-olive for land, grass, animals, haze (#a7b47f / #9da17e / #777a5a). One accent only when the story needs it (our addition: red #ff6a4a). No saturated rainbow.
## 4. Type
Small bilingual subtitle at bottom centre, cream, no box; titles may be formed of dots at the end. In our films: subtitle ≥56 px @1080, typed 35 ms/char.
## 5. Motion
Every dot: per-dot twinkle ≈1.2 Hz random phase (luma ±2–3 %) + slow global breath ≈0.4 Hz (size ±12 %). Forming: dots fly in on bowed arcs with per-dot delay (0–0.35 s), ease-out. Leaving: dots scatter outward & upward, dim, ease-in. Shape morph = same dots re-targeted (never fade-swap). Outline sampling dense (~30 dots / 100×100 px @1080 on figures) vs ambient (2–5 / 100×100).
## 6. Camera
Mostly locked or very slow push/drift; no hard cuts in the reference (0 detected cuts in 50.6 s) — transitions are particle dispersal / regathering and fades to near-black.
## 7. Sound
Soft music, ~−14 LUFS, motion only loosely follows loudness (r ≈ 0.29). In our films: narration + BGM, keyword → element moves on the word.
## 8. Native moves
Scatter-and-regather transition; firefly stream / comet tail of dots; whole figure breathing; dots shiver = itch/anxiety; dots condense = attention.
## 9. Layout
Big negative space; horizon low (bottom 20–30 % land/grass); subject on thirds.
## 10. Engine
canvas 2D, pure function of t, seeded mulberry32; renders via headless Chrome + ffmpeg on the Mac mini (`demo/render_mac.sh`).
## 11. Don'ts
No line strokes (only dots); no hard cuts; no flat fills; don't copy the reference's girl/deer/moon composition.

# Paper Checklist Explainer 清单讲解 — Style Prompt
Status: approved by the owner 2026-11-03. Replaces 红线火柴人.
License boundary: this look is produced with an engine licensed to the owner only. The engine, its source code and its original docs are never shared or published; this entry holds only our own summary, muted previews and keyframes. To make a film in this style you still need the owner's locally installed engine.

## 1. Essence, and what it is not
A vertical explainer that breaks one concept into steps with UI-checklist parts (rounded cards, pill tags, tick lists, bubbles, arrow routes, phone/interface frames) on warm paper, with an original presenter talking from the bottom-right. Not stock motion-graphics templates, not live footage, no logos.
## 2. Materials & rendering
Off-white paper ground with light grain; far layer of pale-grey ridges or mist drifting slowly so the frame is never fully still. Thick ink outlines with offset hard shadows: a paper-cut card feel. Content scaled into the upper-left area to leave the presenter corner free.
## 3. Colour logic
Ink black for outlines and main text; one red for emphasis (keywords, seals, primary buttons, routes); neutral grey only as support. No other hues.
## 4. Type & subtitles
Fonts: Smiley Sans 得意黑 (headlines/captions) and LXGW WenKai 霞鹜文楷 (secondary), both OFL. Captions at the top (~y 330), revealed per character, the spoken character highlighted, keywords red or bold-enlarged. Emphasis devices: tilted red-box "seal", red pill tag, numbered badges 1/2/3. Opinion passages carry a clear red「观点」tag. Brands appear only as text cards.
## 5. Motion quality
Every sentence gets at least one visual action (pop, slide, tick, stamp, connect, count) triggered by a specific spoken character (iron rule). Self-check gates: motion ≥ 4.8, big moments ≥ 0.65/s, calm frames ≤ 27 %, no 2 s gap without a new event. Originality gates: roughly ≥ 40 scene-code lines/s and ≥ 2.5 self-drawn props/mechanisms per second — each script invents its own metaphors.
## 6. Camera grammar
1080×1920, 30 fps, code-only. Safe area y 360–1420; nothing in the right 120 px; bottom-right reserved for the presenter. Light whip between sentences; constant slow push or drift.
## 7. Sound palette
Fish Audio Drama 3 科普男声, whole script in one take, optional slight speed-up (~1.1×; sample_e kept 1.0). Local Whisper per-character alignment checked by CER against the script. Locally synthesized whoosh/pop/ding/stamp SFX on visual events, bus under the voice, near-duplicates merged. Two-pass loudnorm −14 LUFS, TP ≤ −1.5.
## 8. Native moves
Red stamp slam, tick-list fill, numbered badge count, arrow route drawing itself, card flip, presenter pointing at the active card.
## 9. Pitfalls of the medium
Too many reused stock parts fail the originality gate; content under the presenter or caption; dead 2 s stretches; hidden hits during transitions (land the hit before the cut).
## 10. Engine
Owner-licensed local engine (canvas rendering + headless capture + ffmpeg); not shared. Final renders on the Mac mini; one render at a time. Release: H.264 High 4.1 yuv420p tv range CRF 18; mobile CRF 24, ≤3 Mbps, AAC 128k, faststart. Covers 3:4 and 4:3.
## 11. Variation space / known gaps
Presenter: engine-drawn glasses presenter, or the owner's own paper-cut character (sample_e). Pace 20–52 s. Caption lead timing vs on-the-word timing still to settle per film.

## Rules for making a film (owner rules)
1. 12–16 frame stills sheet reviewed before rendering video.
2. Motion and originality gates must pass; at most 4 rounds; never bypass.
3. No upload or publishing until the owner confirms. Facts need sources; no made-up numbers.
